evaluated_target.note: Local develop was synchronized with origin/develop immediately BEFORE the benchmark run began, at the operator's explicit instruction. That state is fixed for the whole run; no fetch, pull, merge, or rebase was performed after benchmark start.

measurement_policy.cpu_contention_note: The host has 8 logical CPUs and 8 GiB RAM. All timed Standard measurements are executed serially with no concurrent agent activity; agent fan-out and timed measurement never overlap.

toolchain_selection_notes.java: The `java` first on PATH was AdoptOpenJDK 8 (x86_64 JRE, no javac, would execute under Rosetta translation). Java is pinned to the native arm64 Homebrew OpenJDK 26.0.1 via JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk for every Java and Kotlin measurement, so Java is measured on a current native JDK rather than a translated legacy JRE.
toolchain_selection_notes.typescript: tsc 7.0.2 removed --outFile; emission uses plain `tsc FILE.ts` and execution uses node.
toolchain_selection_notes.zig: Zig 0.16 replaced the old std.io stdout helpers with an explicit Io instance. Programs use std.Io.Threaded.init_single_threaded and std.Io.File.stdout(); verified working.

frozen_toolchain_recipes._policy: Frozen before any measurement. Every language uses its normal optimized/release build as a competent developer would. Identical in purpose across languages; no language receives benchmark-specific tuning beyond its standard release configuration.
frozen_toolchain_recipes._scope_note: These are the STANDARD-evaluation recipes: each language in the optimized release configuration a competent developer would actually ship. That is what spec section 8 measures. Rust's and Zig's ability to disable checks in release IS a real capability of those languages and is measured as such here; Quidra's lack of an unchecked mode is likewise a real property and its cost is measured, not excused. Primary Evaluation 1 uses `semantic_compression_recipes` instead, for the reason recorded there. The two sets differ ONLY in safety posture, and each is justified by what its evaluation measures.

semantic_compression_recipes._purpose: Frozen build/run recipes used ONLY for Primary Evaluation 1 (Semantic Compression). They differ from the Standard recipes in exactly one controlled variable: SAFETY POSTURE.
semantic_compression_recipes._why_a_separate_set: Semantic Compression asks what the LOCAL SURFACE FORM determines. Probes F08.P1, F08.P2 and F11.P1 ask what happens at integer overflow and at an out-of-bounds index. If Rust is built `-O` (debug assertions silently OFF, so `+` wraps) and Zig `-OReleaseFast` (signed overflow and out-of-bounds are undefined behaviour), while Quidra has only an optimized-AND-checked mode, then those probes score a BUILD FLAG rather than a language's semantics, and they score it against the two languages that offer the choice. Pinning every language that HAS a checked optimized mode into that mode removes the confound. Verified on this host: `rustc -O -C debug-assertions=on` panics on overflow; `zig -OReleaseSafe` traps with 'integer overflow'. C++ has no checked mode and is recorded as such -- that is a language fact, scored by metrics B and D, not smuggled in through the recipe.
